title: Magnitude 5.2 Earthquake Strikes Alaska
subtitle: A 10 km deep tremor occurred on September 3, 2026
excerpt: A magnitude 5.2 earthquake was recorded 100 km south-southwest of Nikolski, Alaska, at 10:03 AM (Brasília time).
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A magnitude 5.2 earthquake occurred 100 km south-southwest of Nikolski, Alaska, at 10:03 AM on September 3, 2026 (Brasília time). The epicenter was located at a depth of 10 km.

Earthquake Fact Sheet

Data released by the United States Geological Survey (USGS) indicates that the tremor did not generate an impact alert, but was accompanied by a tsunami warning. There were no recorded reports of people who felt the tremor.

Tsunami Warning

The USGS issued a tsunami warning for the coastal region near the epicenter. To date, there is no public information regarding observed waves or evacuations.

Absence of Felt Reports

According to the USGS report, no resident or visitor in the area reported perceiving the seismic movement. This may be related to the focal depth and the low population density of the region.

Official Response and Monitoring

Local authorities have not yet released official statements regarding response measures or damage assessments. The USGS will continue monitoring seismic activity in the zone and will update data as new information becomes available.

Next Steps

With the lack of reports of direct impact, investigations are focusing on verifying possible alterations to the seabed that could generate tsunami waves. Monitoring by regional seismic networks remains active to detect any potential aftershocks.

Seismic data: USGS.
